ABSTRACT  
15 July 2020  
Keywords:  
Derivation,  
Verbs, African, Masaaba. In this article, the researcher explains how verbs in African languages are derived to convey different meanings. This is done by referring to Masaaba, a language spoken by the Masaaba people in Uganda. Verb derivation is a common phenomenon and is practiced in various languages. Therefore, in this article, the researcher describes the verb derivation process in the Masaaba language. He presents a collection of verbs and explains how speakers derive them. In addition, the researcher discusses how these verbs are used in sentences. The researcher does this because many African languages have not been studied, and there are many fascinating aspects that are unknown to the world. In this work, the researcher writes various verbs in the original language and then translates them into Swahili. The aim of this study is, firstly, to demonstrate the process of verb derivation in Masaaba; secondly, to explain the different meanings that result from verb derivation; and thirdly, to show that Masaaba is a language that continues to grow like other African languages. The research approach was field-based. Using this approach, the researcher visited the field where they conducted interviews with their respondents. The responses of the respondents constituted the data needed by the researcher. In conclusion, the findings of this research indicate that Kimasaaba, like other African languages, has a great number of verbs that are derived and facilitate the speakers’ discourse. A verb is a word that describes the state of an action. A single verb can be derived and express different states of actions. Typically, there are forms such as the active, reciprocal, passive, stative, and causative in many Bantu languages. Therefore, in this work, the researcher lists various Kimasaaba verbs, which is the language of the Bamasaaba, and translates them into Swahili. It should be noted early on that there are different dialects of Kimasaaba. Therefore, in this research, the researcher focused on a particular dialect known as ‘Lubuuya.’ After translating the verbs, the researcher explains the process of verb derivation. Having described how these verbs are derived, the researcher clarifies how they are used in sentences. The researcher does so by considering the explanations of various authors regarding verb derivation. Finally, the researcher concludes the work by providing his views on important matters related to the research. RESEARCH QUESTION  
In this study, the researcher employed the interview method. Using this approach, the researcher went out into the field to meet the respondents. Before conducting the interviews, the researcher explained to the respondents the purpose of the research. After doing so, the researcher proceeded to conduct interviews with them. The respondents consisted of 50 women and 50 men. The researcher ensured that there was an equal number of women and men due to the issue of gender equality. These respondents were selected using the purposive sampling method. Using this method, the researcher continued conversations with the respondents as he met them. He did not use any special procedure in selecting the respondents. The researcher had a set of questions that he used during the interviews. The researcher used this guide to ensure that he would not forget any important points. The discussions that were conducted largely focused on verb derivation. After mentioning a verb, the researcher asked how to derive it in different contexts. According to the researcher, there are very many ethnic groups in Africa. Each ethnic group has its own indigenous language. Therefore, there are numerous languages spoken across the continent. However, the majority of these languages have not been researched, and there is a great deal that these languages convey which is still unknown to the world. There are very few African languages that have been thoroughly studied.

In grammar, derivation is the ability of a root or stem to be affixed with a morpheme at its beginning or end. The result is to expand the meaning of the given word. This is the function of every affix—to build new roots and stems of words, which are called derivational stems or roots. We can also say that this is the function of derivational affixes or formative affixes. Often, formative affixes appear at the end of the stem or root. Accordingly, they have continued to be called suffix-formative affixes. In this context, derivation involves two types of affixes: (a) Semantic Affixes, which appear at the beginning of the root of a word. These affixes can expand the meaning of a word without changing its root. For example: tu-ta-m-pig-an-ish-a. A participial verb, which takes the same form as “ni” or “si”, is considered to link other elements in a sentence. Example: Musa is a teacher, the town of Msoma is smaller than the town of Mwanza, this young man is not honest, I am not a student. Based on the context of these sentences, it appears that these elements are considered to link the constituents on the left and right sides of the verb itself. These sentences are in the present tense. If these sentences are changed to different tenses, the participial verbs within them (that is, “ni” and “si”) change and take the form of the verb “kuwa,” as seen in these examples: Musa was a teacher, the town of Msoma was smaller than the town of Mwanza, this young man was not honest, I was not a student. We see here that: (i) -pig- is the root of the word tutampiganisha. (ii) tu-ta-m- are the affixes that come before the root –pig-. (iii) –an-ish-a are the affixes that come after the root –pig-. The prefixes and suffixes of the root -pig- give different meanings, as follows: (i) The prefix tu- indicates first person plural (we). (ii) The prefix -ta- indicates future tense. (iii) The prefix -m- refers to the object, third person singular (him/her). (iv) The affix -an- indicates reciprocity. (v) The affix –ish- is the causative marker. (vi) The affix -a is for finalizing the verb form. (b) Derivational or formative affixes normally occur at the end of the stem of the word. According to these scholars, a verb is a word that describes an action. The verb carries the noun and indicates what it wants to do and at what time. However, derivation is the process of increasing a word’s ability to be used in various contexts and generating new vocabulary different from the original, even though its root remains unchanged. Also, derivation refers to words that share the same root but can distinguish themselves through different forms and generate new vocabulary. These affixes serve three functions: (i) to expand the meaning of a word, (ii) to construct the root or stem for derivation, and (iii) to change a word from one class to another. Vitenzi, Mwafrika, Masaaba. Katika makala haya, mtafiti anaeleza jinsi vitenzi katika lugha za Kiafrika vinavyotolewa ili kuleta maana mbalimbali. Hilo linafanywa kwa kurejelea Kimasaaba, lugha inayozungumzwa na Wamasaaba nchini Uganda. Unyambulishaji wa vitenzi ni jambo la kawaida na hutekelezwa katika lugha mbalimbali. Kwa kuhitimisha, matokeo ya utafiti huu yanaonyesha kuwa Kimasaaba, kama lugha nyingine za Kiafrika, ina idadi kubwa ya vitenzi vinavyotoholewa na kuwezesha mazungumzo ya wazungumzaji. Kutokana na pengo hili, mtafiti aliamua kuendeleza utafiti huu kwa lengo la kubainisha hali halisi ya Kimasaaba. Hii ni kwa sababu lugha nyingi za walio wachache zimetoweka kutokana na kutofanyiwa utafiti, na nyingine zinaendelea kutoweka. MBINU ZA UTAFITI  
Kitenzi ni neno linaloelezea hali ya kitendo. Kitenzi kimoja kinaweza kutolewa na kueleza hali tofauti za vitendo. Kwa kawaida, kuna maumbo kama vile amilifu, wasilianifu, hali ya hali ya hewa, hali na visababishi katika lugha nyingi za Kibantu. Kwa hivyo, katika kazi hii, mtafiti ameorodhesha vitenzi mbalimbali vya Kimasaaba ambayo ni lugha ya Wabamasaaba na kuvitafsiri katika Kiswahili. Ikumbukwe mapema kwamba kuna lahaja mbalimbali za Kimasaaba. Kwa hiyo, katika utafiti huu, mtafiti alijikita katika lahaja fulani ijulikanayo kwa jina la ‘Lubuuya.’ Baada ya kutafsiri vitenzi, mtafiti anaeleza mchakato wa unyambulishaji wa vitenzi. Baada ya kueleza jinsi vitenzi hivi vinavyotolewa, mtafiti anafafanua jinsi vinavyotumika katika sentensi. Mtafiti hufanya hivyo kwa kuzingatia maelezo ya waandishi mbalimbali kuhusu unyambulishaji wa vitenzi. Hatimaye, mtafiti anahitimisha kazi kwa kutoa maoni yake kuhusu mambo muhimu yanayohusiana na utafiti. SWALI LA UTAFITI  
Katika utafiti huu, mtafiti alitumia mbinu ya usaili. Kwa kutumia mbinu hii, mtafiti alikwenda uwanjani kukutana na watafitiwa. Kabla ya kufanya mahojiano, mtafiti aliwaeleza watafitiwa madhumuni ya utafiti. Baada ya kufanya hivyo, mtafiti aliendelea na mahojiano nao. Waliohojiwa walikuwa wanawake 50 na wanaume 50. Mtafiti alihakikisha kuwa kuna idadi sawa ya wanawake na wanaume kutokana na suala la usawa wa kijinsia. Wahojiwa hawa walichaguliwa kwa kutumia mbinu madhubuti ya sampuli. Kwa kutumia mbinu hii, mtafiti aliendelea na mazungumzo na watafitiwa alipokutana nao. Hakutumia utaratibu maalum katika kuchagua wahojiwa. Mtafiti alikuwa na seti ya maswali ambayo alitumia wakati wa mahojiano. Mtafiti alitumia mwongozo huu ili kuhakikisha kwamba hatasahau mambo yoyote muhimu. Majadiliano ambayo yaliendeshwa kwa kiasi kikubwa yalilenga unyambulishaji wa vitenzi. Baada ya kutaja kitenzi, mtafiti aliuliza jinsi ya kukiibua katika miktadha tofauti. Kulingana na mtafiti huyo, kuna makabila mengi sana barani Afrika. Kila kabila lina lugha yake ya asili. Kwa hiyo, kuna lugha nyingi zinazozungumzwa katika bara zima. Hata hivyo, lugha nyingi kati ya hizi hazijafanyiwa utafiti, na kuna mengi ambayo lugha hizi huwasilisha ambayo bado haijulikani kwa ulimwengu. Kuna lugha chache sana za Kiafrika ambazo zimesomwa kwa kina.

Anasema zaidi kwamba kwa kupata vitenzi, tunapata maumbo mbalimbali ya vitenzi, ambayo ni: kiambishi, tendaji, kitendeshi, kisababishi, kiima, kiarifu, na kiambishi cha pande zote. a) tungua + a b) tungo + e + a c) tungo + ele +a d) subiri + ele +an +a e) subiri +ez +a f) subiri +ez +esh + a g) subiri +ez +esh +an +a  
Katamba (2003) anaeleza kuwa uasiliaji kama unavyodhihirika katika lugha za Kibantu na lugha nyinginezo ni mchakato unaozalisha aina mpya za maneno au kuongeza maana mahususi kwenye mzizi au shina. Kwa mfano, kutoka kwenye mzizi nguruwe-, tunapata neno ‘piga’ ambalo ni kitenzi. Na tukipata neno hili, tunapata maneno kama vile pigana, piganisha, pigika, ambayo kila moja ina maana tofauti. Kutoka kwa mzizi wa kitenzi tungo-, tunaweza kupata maneno kama yale yaliyoorodheshwa hapo juu, ambapo viambishi tamati –e, -an, -ele, -esh ni unyago, kwani huufanya maumbo yanayozungumziwa kuwa vitenzi vyenye maana tofauti. Kiswahili kina viambishi tamati vinane vya vitenzi ambavyo vimeambatishwa kwenye mizizi ya vitenzi kwa namna iliyoonyeshwa hapo juu. Viambatisho vya viambishi ni kama vifuatavyo: (a). -w (b) -ik / -ek (c) -ish-/-iz-/-esh-/-ez- (d) -il- (e) -o-/-u (f) -am- (g) -an- (h) -at Wahiga (1999) anaeleza kuwa neno 'unyambulishaji' linatokana na vitenzi viwili.
TUKI (2004) inaeleza kuwa unyambulishaji ni mchakato wa kuongeza viambishi katika vitenzi ili kuleta maana mbalimbali. Utaratibu huu ndio unaojulikana kama unyambulishaji wa vitenzi. Kulingana na wataalamu hawa, kitenzi kina sehemu kuu ambayo ni mzizi, na huruhusu kuongezwa kwa viambishi mwanzoni au mwishoni. Matei (2008) anaeleza kuwa kati ya aina zote za maneno, kitenzi ndicho kinachoonyesha kitendo kilichofanywa au kinachofanywa. Anaendelea kueleza kuwa kitenzi kinaweza kuonyesha hali mbalimbali kutokana na unyambulishaji. Ameweza kuainisha vitenzi katika makundi mawili: vitenzi vya kutenda na vitenzi vinavyoashiria umilikaji. Kihore na wenzake (2003) wanagawanya vitenzi katika aina kuu tatu: kitenzi kikuu (T), kitenzi kisaidizi (Ts), na kitenzi kishirikishi (t). Wanaeleza kuwa kitenzi kikuu ni kitenzi ambacho kinaweza kujitokeza kikijitegemea katika sentensi na kukamilisha maana kikiwa peke yake. Kwa mfano: amelala, tutampiga Juma, Khamis atamuona Musa kesho. Kitenzi kisaidizi ni kitenzi kinachojitokeza pamoja na kitenzi kikuu katika sentensi, kama katika mifano ifuatayo: alikuwa analala (alikuwa amelala), tunapenda kula (tunapenda kula), Juma alitaka kutudhulumu mali yetu (Juma alitaka kututapeli mali yetu). Mifano hii inaonyesha kwamba kwa kawaida vitenzi visaidizi huja kwanza, vikifuatiwa na vitenzi vikuu. Mwaka wa 2008, uasilia ni neno ambalo maana yake inatokana na maana za maneno mawili: (i) “Kunyambua,” ambayo ina maana ya kukata vipande vipande; (ii) “Kunyumbua,” kumaanisha kunyoosha na kuvuta kitu chenye kunyumbulika, mfano kamba ya raba. Katika sarufi, unyambulishaji ni uwezo wa mzizi au shina kupachikwa na mofimu mwanzoni au mwisho wake. Matokeo yake ni kupanua maana ya neno lililotolewa. Hii ndiyo kazi ya kila kiambishi—kujenga mizizi na mashina mapya ya maneno, ambayo huitwa mashina au mizizi. Tunaweza pia kusema kwamba hii ni kazi ya viambishi vya viambishi au viambishi muundo. Mara nyingi, viambishi vya uundaji vinaonekana mwishoni mwa shina au mzizi. Kwa hiyo, zimeendelea kuitwa viambishi tamati vya kiambishi. Katika muktadha huu, unyambulishaji unahusisha aina mbili za viambishi: (a) Viambishi vya Semantiki, ambavyo hujitokeza mwanzoni mwa mzizi wa neno. Viambishi hivi vinaweza kupanua maana ya neno bila kubadilisha mzizi wake. Kwa mfano: tu-ta-m-pig-an-ish-a. Kitenzi kishirikishi, ambacho huchukua umbo sawa na "ni" au "si", huzingatiwa kuunganisha vipengele vingine katika sentensi. Mfano: Musa ni mwalimu, mji wa Msoma ni mdogo kuliko mji wa Mwanza, huyu kijana si mwaminifu, mimi si mwanafunzi. Kulingana na muktadha wa sentensi hizi, inaonekana kwamba vipengele hivi vinazingatiwa kuunganisha viambajengo vya upande wa kushoto na kulia wa kitenzi chenyewe. Sentensi hizi ziko katika wakati uliopo. Sentensi hizi zikibadilishwa kuwa nyakati tofauti, vitenzi vishirikishi vilivyomo ndani yake (yaani, “ni” na “si”) hubadilika na kuchukua umbo la kitenzi “kuwa,” inavyoonekana katika mifano hii: Musa alikuwa mwalimu, mji wa Msoma ulikuwa mdogo kuliko mji wa Mwanza, kijana huyu hakuwa mwaminifu, mimi sikuwa mwanafunzi. Tunaona hapa kwamba: (i) -pig- ni mzizi wa neno tutampiganisha. (ii) tu-ta-m- ni viambishi vinavyokuja kabla ya mzizi -pig-. (iii) –an-ish-a ni viambishi vinavyokuja baada ya mzizi –pig-. Keywords:  
Derivation,  
Verbs, African, Masaaba. In this article, the researcher explains how verbs in African languages are derived to convey different meanings. This is done by referring to Masaaba, a language spoken by the Masaaba people in Uganda. Verb derivation is a common phenomenon and is practiced in various languages. Therefore, in this article, the researcher describes the verb derivation process in the Masaaba language. He presents a collection of verbs and explains how speakers derive them. In addition, the researcher discusses how these verbs are used in sentences. The researcher does this because many African languages have not been studied, and there are many fascinating aspects that are unknown to the world. In this work, the researcher writes various verbs in the original language and then translates them into Swahili. The aim of this study is, firstly, to demonstrate the process of verb derivation in Masaaba; secondly, to explain the different meanings that result from verb derivation; and thirdly, to show that Masaaba is a language that continues to grow like other African languages.

RESEARCH METHODS  
A verb is a word that describes the state of an action. A single verb can be derived and express different states of actions. Typically, there are forms such as the active, reciprocal, passive, stative, and causative in many Bantu languages. Therefore, in this work, the researcher lists various Kimasaaba verbs, which is the language of the Bamasaaba, and translates them into Swahili. It should be noted early on that there are different dialects of Kimasaaba. Therefore, in this research, the researcher focused on a particular dialect known as ‘Lubuuya.’ After translating the verbs, the researcher explains the process of verb derivation. Having described how these verbs are derived, the researcher clarifies how they are used in sentences. The researcher does so by considering the explanations of various authors regarding verb derivation. Finally, the researcher concludes the work by providing his views on important matters related to the research.

Mbwillow (2017) explains that words in human languages are formed in various ways. He mentions methods such as reduplication, coining, compounding, and affixation, referring specifically to inflection and derivation. He explains that affixation is the process of attaching or adding morphemes or affixes before or after the root, core, or stem of a word. He emphasizes that the main methods of word formation are inflection and derivation. He defines derivation as the process of attaching morphemes/affixes after the root and stem of a word. In his work, he states that inflection and derivation form new words. He clarifies that inflection and derivation may not necessarily change the word class but rather expand the meaning of the word in question. This includes the possibility for the action of a verb to be possible, for example: someka, imbika, ombeka, fungika.

discourses.source_txt: The literature also shows that there are many scholars who have written about verb derivation in languages. Some scholars have written about verb derivation in the Swahili language, while others have written about verb derivation in other African languages such as Kinyakyusa, Kigiryama, Kigichugu, and so on.
discourses.translated_txt: Fasihi pia inaonyesha kwamba kuna wataalamu wengi ambao wameandika kuhusu unyambulishaji wa vitenzi katika lugha. discourses.source_txt: The writings of various scholars demonstrate that a verb is a word that expresses an action, whereas derivation is the process of adding affixes to a verb to generate new words with different meanings. Various texts also indicate that there are different types of verb derivation. These types include the active voice, the applicative, the reciprocal, the stative, the causative, and the mutual applicative forms.

Kutokana na matokeo ya utafiti huu, ni wazi kuwa lugha za Kiafrika, hasa lugha za Kibantu, zinaruhusu matumizi ya uambishaji wa vitenzi.

discourses.source_txt: Kimasaaba, as one of the African languages, does allow for verb inflection. This verb inflection facilitates communication with ease. This is because speakers of the language can use a single word to convey different meanings. If speakers of the language do not have the ability to inflect verbs, they will not be fully proficient in the grammar of Kiswahili: questions and exercises.
discourses.translated_txt: Kimasaaba, kama mojawapo ya lugha za Kiafrika, hairuhusu uambishaji wa vitenzi. Unyambulishaji huu wa vitenzi hurahisisha mawasiliano kwa urahisi. Hii ni kwa sababu wazungumzaji wa lugha wanaweza kutumia neno moja ili kuleta maana tofauti. Iwapo wazungumzaji wa lugha hiyo hawana uwezo wa kuawilisha vitenzi, hawatakuwa na ujuzi kamili wa sarufi ya Kiswahili: maswali na mazoezi.
